title: Ephemeral NAT reuse during autoscaler scale-down leads to cross-tenant DNS misassociation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Production customer escalations reported intermittent DNS responses resolving to the wrong tenant after aggressive autoscaler scale-downs on Dedicated clusters. Investigation shows ephemeral NAT (ephemeral port) reuse combined with a delayed conntrack cleanup and a route programming race resulted in DNS replies being associated with stale socket contexts and thus delivered to an unrelated tenant's ephemeral flow. The bug surfaced under bursty workloads and rapid scale-down policies configured by some customers.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision Dedicated pool with per-tenant overlay and autoscaler configured with aggressive scale-down (scale-down-delay <= 30s)
Generate bursty outbound DNS traffic from two tenants simultaneously (UDP queries to shared resolver)
Trigger rapid scale-down by idle-check cycling or simulated low load
Observe occasional DNS responses arriving over connections associated with a different tenant or connection context
Collect conntrack and SNAT table snapshots from host and verify ephemeral port reuse timestamps
observations: conntrack entries were not consistently removed during scale-down due to controller race with route teardown
SNAT ephemeral port pools are shared at host level and were reallocated quickly causing reuse within the kernel's 1-2 second window
DNS resolver affinity at the controller level relied on endpoint ephemeral ports rather than a tenant-scoped tag
Customers with more aggressive scale-down settings were more likely to surface the issue
No evidence of data exfiltration; this was misassociation of UDP replies at network level
mitigation: Immediate: advise affected customers to increase scale-down delay to 120s as temporary mitigation
Immediate: apply per-tenant SNAT pool limit via iptables/netfilter rules on customer hosts (hotfix script) for high-risk clusters
Short-term: deploy controller change to add a 5s grace before conntrack flush when route teardown is initiated
Medium-term: introduce tenant-scoped resolver affinity tags so DNS replies are matched to tenant context regardless of ephemeral port reuse
postmortem_findings: Root cause: controller route teardown raced with conntrack removal and SNAT reallocation. The kernel's ephemeral port reuse semantics combined with our host-level shared SNAT pools allowed a short window for cross-tenant UDP reply misassociation.
We lacked tenant-scoped invariants in the DNS resolver affinity logic which made it possible for replies to be matched by ephemeral port alone.
Monitoring gap: no existing metric flagged rapid-scale down induced conntrack churn; added new metric counters for conntrack_deletions_per_tenant and snat_reuse_rate
resolution_summary: Implemented controller-side 5s conntrack grace on route teardown, added tenant-scoped resolver affinity tags, and deployed host hotfix to isolate SNAT pools per tenant. Rolled out to 20% of clusters, monitored for 48h with no recurrence. Plan full rollout over next week and customer-facing postmortem published.
rollout_plan: Canary: runtime + networking-agent changes to 10% of Dedicated clusters (2/2025-02-21)
Gradual: increase to 50% after 72h if stable, then full rollout to remaining clusters
Follow-up: add e2e test covering scale-down DNS flows and include in CI gating
next_steps: Complete code review feedback on runtime PR (addressed by @marco Fernandez)
Finish automation for per-tenant SNAT allocation in host-init scripts
Add CI e2e test and flake detection for DNS misassociation scenarios
Schedule post-release 1-week verification and contact affected customers with remediation summary
